newsitem.title: UK: UK awards 25 offshore oil permits, snubs Greenpeace.
newsitem.headline: UK awards 25 offshore oil permits, snubs Greenpeace.

text.p: Britain on Monday awarded 25 permits to 14 operators to explore for oil on the U.K. Continental Shelf but rejected a bid by environmental group Greenpeace for all 22,000 square miles offered under the 17th licensing round.

Energy minister Richard Page said the majority of the tranches awarded, covering 76 blocks, are for acreage west of the Hebrides, seven are north of the Shetland Islands and the remaining four are in the southern North Sea.
Environmental lobby group Greenpeace, which had bid for all the acreage on offer in the hope of turning it into a marine wildlife sanctuary, was unsuccessful.
"One organisation applied to undertake work that does not require a petroleum production licence," the Department of Trade and Industry said.
"This did not represent a valid application and its application fee is being returned."

The successful operators are: Murphy Petroleum Ltd, British Ltd, British Gas, Fina Petroleum, Texaco Britain Ltd, Marathon Oil UK Ltd, Enterprise Oil plc, Phillips Petroleum, Conoco (UK) Ltd, Elf Exploration, Mobil North Sea and Shell UK Ltd.
The 25 tranches were awarded to the operators and a total of 22 partners, the DTI said.

Licences awarded under the 17th licensing round are valid initially for three years, during which an agreed programme or exploration work has to be carried out. Companies may extend the licence for a further six years providing that additional exploration work is carried out.

Earlier this month, Greenpeace made an official complaint to the European Commission calling for the 17th round to be blocked because, it claimed, environmental assessments required under a 1985 EU directive had not been carried out.
